literature.headline_zh: 发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 临床判定的心源性休克发生在143名患者(18.5%)中;在164例院内死亡患者中,99例(60.4%)为CS患者。生物标志物轨迹分析显示,发展为CS的患者中炎症、心脏、肾脏和凝血标志物持续升高,而脂质标志物显示时间依赖性下降。 [10.1186/s12879-026-14600-z]
该Gn-LFA检测了在哺乳动物和植物表达系统中产生的重组Gn蛋白,并在多种宿主宿主的血清中表现出兼容性。 [10.1186/s12985-026-03329-5]
使用针对发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒(SFTSV)S、M和L基因组片段的混合crRNA,该检测方法在三个重复实验中均检测到了最低测试输入浓度10.38 fM。 [10.1016/j.bios.2026.119326]
代谢组学分析显示色氨酸代谢显著紊乱:L-色氨酸水平降低,而色氨酮及其下游代谢产物(色氨酮酸[KA]、3-羟基邻氨基苯甲酸[3-HAA]、黄尿酸[XA]和5-羟基吲哚乙酸[5-HIP])水平升高,提示色氨酮通路被激活。 [10.3389/fimmu.2026.1898053]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.headline_en: Recent Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus literature
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: Clinically adjudicated CS occurred in 143 patients (18.5%); among 164 in-hospital deaths, 99 (60.4%) occurred in patients with CS. [10.1186/s12879-026-14600-z]

Vaccination markedly reduced mortality (RR = 0.10, 95% CI 0.05–0.21), post-challenge weight loss (RR = 0.21, 95% CI 0.12–0.37), and detectable viremia (RR = 0.45, 95% CI 0.27–0.73), although the effect estimate was attenuated in the trim-and-fill sensitivity analysis (RR = 0.74, 95% CI: 0.36–1.51). [10.3389/fmicb.2026.1978600]
The Gn-LFA detected recombinant Gn proteins produced in both mammalian and plant expression systems and demonstrated compatibility across sera from multiple host species. [10.1186/s12985-026-03329-5]

Using pooled crRNAs targeting the S, M, and L genomic segments of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV), the assay detected the lowest tested input concentration of 10.38 fM in all three replicates. [10.1016/j.bios.2026.119326]

Metabolomic profiling revealed marked disruption of tryptophan metabolism: L-tryptophan levels were decreased, whereas kynurenine and its downstream metabolites (kynurenic acid [KA], 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid [3-HAA], xanthurenic acid [XA], and 5-hydroxyindolepyruvate [5-HIP]) were increased, suggesting activation of the kynurenine pathway. [10.3389/fimmu.2026.1898053]
literature.trend_or_risk_en: The direction of this week's research is defined by the clinical, epidemiological, ecological, diagnostic and molecular topics actually represented by the eligible publications.
literature.brief_en: This literature brief prioritizes papers published in the active reporting window and ranks them by relevance, evidence availability, study quality, recency, and independent-source convergence. Detailed study-specific evidence is retained in the article cards below.
brief_items_zh: 本期发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
临床判定的心源性休克发生在143名患者(18.5%)中;在164例院内死亡患者中,99例(60.4%)为CS患者。生物标志物轨迹分析显示,发展为CS的患者中炎症、心脏、肾脏和凝血标志物持续升高,而脂质标志物显示时间依赖性下降。
该Gn-LFA检测了在哺乳动物和植物表达系统中产生的重组Gn蛋白,并在多种宿主宿主的血清中表现出兼容性。 [10.1186/s12985-026-03329-5]。
使用针对发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒(SFTSV)S、M和L基因组片段的混合crRNA,该检测方法在三个重复实验中均检测到了最低测试输入浓度10.38 fM。 [10.1016/j.bios.2026.119326]。
代谢组学分析显示色氨酸代谢显著紊乱:L-色氨酸水平降低,而色氨酮及其下游代谢产物(色氨酮酸[KA]、3-羟基邻氨基苯甲酸[3-HAA]、黄尿酸[XA]和5-羟基吲哚乙酸[5-HIP])水平升高,提示色氨酮通路被激活。
brief_items_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
Clinically adjudicated CS occurred in 143 patients (18.5%); among 164 in-hospital deaths, 99 (60.4%) occurred in patients with CS. [10.1186/s12879-026-14600-z].

Vaccination markedly reduced mortality (RR = 0.10, 95% CI 0.05–0.21), post-challenge weight loss (RR = 0.21, 95% CI 0.12–0.37), and detectable viremia (RR = 0.45, 95% CI 0.27–0.73), although the effect estimate was attenuated in the trim-and-fill sensitivity analysis (RR = 0.74, 95% CI: 0.36–1.51).

The Gn-LFA detected recombinant Gn proteins produced in both mammalian and plant expression systems and demonstrated compatibility across sera from multiple host species. [10.1186/s12985-026-03329-5].

Using pooled crRNAs targeting the S, M, and L genomic segments of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV), the assay detected the lowest tested input concentration of 10.38 fM in all three replicates.

news.headline_zh: 发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: 一个研究小组使用针对病毒 Gn 糖蛋白的单克隆抗体开发了一种针对 发热伴血小板减少综合征 病毒 (SFTSV) 的快速磁力侧流检测。该测试旨在在 45 分钟内检测出病毒,无需实验室设备、电力或专门仪器。据报道,这一进展是提高 SFTSV 诊断能力的重要一步。 [news-2bd9c59ffcce3e83]
现代生物科学正在将其 抗病毒药物 候选药物 XAFTY 推进 发热伴血小板减少综合征 的 2 期临床试验,发热伴血小板减少综合征 是一种 蜱媒 疾病,在韩国尚未获得批准的 治疗。该公司计划向韩国食品药品安全部提交新药研究申请。 [news-c295343aa4e3f1c6]
所提供的证据在验证的英文中并未明确报告核心事件。 [news-2b3c1231d76e6312]
BMC Infectiousdies 上发表的一项回顾性研究发现,心源性休克是 发热伴血小板减少综合征 患者致命结果的主要最终途径,有 143 名患者 (18.5%) 出现这种情况,其中 99 名 (60%) 在医院死亡。 [news-b3740ede0debdb21]
现代生物科学宣布计划将其 抗病毒药物 候选药物 XAFTY 推进 发热伴血小板减少综合征 的 治疗 的 2 期临床试验,发热伴血小板减少综合征 是一种尚未获得批准治疗的 蜱媒 疾病。 [news-c65c4db54c197823]

news.headline_en: Recent Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus news
news.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus news developments.
key_findings_en: A research team developed a rapid magnetic lateral flow test for SFTS virus (SFTSV) using monoclonal antibodies against the viral Gn glycoprotein. The test is designed to detect the virus within 45 minutes without requiring laboratory equipment, electricity, or specialized instrumentation. [news-2bd9c59ffcce3e83]

Hyundai Bioscience is advancing its antiviral candidate XAFTY into Phase 2 clinical trials for SFTS, a tick-borne disease with no approved treatment in South Korea. The company plans to submit its investigational new drug application to South Korea's Ministry of Food and Drug Safety. [news-c295343aa4e3f1c6]
The supplied evidence does not clearly report the central event in verified English. [news-2b3c1231d76e6312]

A retrospective study published in BMC Infectious Diseases identified cardiogenic shock as a dominant final pathway for fatal outcomes in SFTS patients, with 143 patients (18.5%) developing the condition and 99 of them (60%) dying in the hospital. [news-b3740ede0debdb21]

Hyundai Bioscience announced plans to advance its antiviral drug candidate XAFTY into Phase 2 clinical trials for the treatment of SFTS, a tick-borne disease with no approved therapy available. [news-c65c4db54c197823]

papers.title: Efficacy of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome vaccines in animal models: a systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.abstract: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is an emerging tick-borne zoonosis that threatens both animal and human health across East Asia, yet no licensed vaccine is currently available. We therefore conducted a PRISMA-guided systematic review and meta-analysis of preclinical murine and ferret studies to evaluate severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus vaccine efficacy. Seven electronic databases were searched for studies published between 2009 and 2025. Random-effects meta-analyses evaluated mortality, viremia, and post-challenge weight loss. Quantitative viral burden was further evaluated using standardized mean differences for mean and peak viremia, whereas body-weight trajectories were assessed using generalized linear mixed models. Twenty-three studies met the inclusion criteria. Vaccination markedly reduced mortality (RR = 0.10, 95% CI 0.05–0.21), post-challenge weight loss (RR = 0.21, 95% CI 0.12–0.37), and detectable viremia (RR = 0.45, 95% CI 0.27–0.73), although the effect estimate was attenuated in the trim-and-fill sensitivity analysis (RR = 0.74, 95% CI: 0.36–1.51). Furthermore, significantly suppressing both mean and peak viremia under homologous and heterologous challenge conditions. Longitudinal analyses further demonstrated improved preservation of body weight, particularly following mRNA and vector vaccination. These findings provide the strongest quantitative evidence supporting the development of broadly protective SFTSV vaccines for both human and veterinary use within a One Health framework.

Seven electronic databases were searched for studies published between 2009 and 2025. Random-effects meta-analyses evaluated mortality, viremia, and post-challenge weight loss. Quantitative viral burden was further evaluated using standardized mean differences for mean and peak viremia, whereas body-weight trajectories were assessed using generalized linear mixed models. Twenty-three studies met the inclusion criteria. Vaccination markedly reduced mortality (RR = 0.10, 95% CI 0.05–0.21), post-challenge weight loss (RR = 0.21, 95% CI 0.12–0.37), and detectable viremia (RR = 0.45, 95% CI 0.27–0.73), although the effect estimate was attenuated in the trim-and-fill sensitivity analysis (RR = 0.74, 95% CI: 0.36–1.51). Furthermore, significantly suppressing both mean and peak viremia under homologous and heterologous challenge conditions. Longitudinal analyses further demonstrated improved preservation of body weight, particularly following mRNA and vector vaccination. These findings provide the strongest quantitative evidence supporting the development of broadly protective SFTSV vaccines for both human and veterinary use within a One Health framework.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates the efficacy of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV) vaccines in preclinical animal models. The review included 23 studies from seven databases, published between 2009 and 2025, and used random-effects meta-analyses to assess mortality, viremia, and post-challenge weight loss. Vaccination significantly reduced mortality (RR = 0.10, 95% CI 0.05–0.21), post-challenge weight loss (RR = 0.21, 95% CI 0.12–0.37), and detectable viremia (RR = 0.45, 95% CI 0.27–0.73), although the effect estimate was weakened in trim-and-fill sensitivity analysis. Longitudinal analyses showed improved body weight preservation, especially with mRNA and vector vaccines. The findings support the development of broadly protective SFTSV vaccines for human and veterinary use, emphasizing the need for further research in natural host populations and field settings.

papers.abstract: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV) is an emerging tick-borne zoonotic pathogen associated with high mortality in humans and silent circulation in animals, highlighting the need for rapid, field-deployable diagnostics. Current molecular and serological methods remain dependent on specialized infrastructure, limiting their use in resource-limited settings. Here, we developed a magnetic nanoparticle-enhanced lateral flow assay targeting the SFTSV glycoprotein Gn (Gn-LFA) for rapid antigen detection. A panel of anti-Gn monoclonal antibodies was generated and systematically characterized for isotype, epitope recognition, binding affinity, and viral capture efficiency. A monoclonal antibody exhibiting strong Gn recognition and antigen-capturing activity was selected as the detection antibody and conjugated to magnetic nanoparticles, while three additional antibodies were used as capture antibodies on the test line to improve antigen recognition. The Gn-LFA detected recombinant Gn proteins produced in both mammalian and plant expression systems and demonstrated compatibility across sera from multiple host species. The assay detected as little as 20 ng of recombinant Gn protein or approximately 5 × 10 5 FFU of SFTSV within 45 min without requiring specialized instrumentation. Collectively, this study provides proof of concept for a rapid and low-cost approach to SFTSV antigen detection and supports its further development for potential applications in resource-limited settings and One Health surveillance.

papers.abstract_zh: 发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒(SFTSV)是一种新兴的蜱媒人兽共患病原体,与人类高死亡率和动物中的无声传播有关,凸显了快速、现场可部署诊断方法的必要性。目前的分子和血清学方法仍依赖于专门的基础设施,限制了其在资源有限环境中的应用。在此,我们开发了一种针对SFTSV糖蛋白Gn的磁性纳米粒子增强型侧向流动检测方法(Gn-LFA),用于快速抗原检测。我们生成并系统地表征了一组抗Gn单克隆抗体,包括Ig类型、表位识别、结合亲和力和病毒捕获效率。选择了一种具有强Gn识别能力和抗原捕获活性的单克隆抗体作为检测抗体,并将其偶联到磁性纳米粒子上,同时使用三种额外的抗体作为测试线上的捕获抗体以提高抗原识别能力。该Gn-LFA检测了在哺乳动物和植物表达系统中产生的重组Gn蛋白,并在多种宿主宿主的血清中表现出兼容性。该检测方法在45分钟内无需专门仪器即可检测到20 ng的重组Gn蛋白或约5 × 10^5 FFU的SFTSV。总体而言,本研究为SFTSV抗原检测提供了一种快速且低成本的方法概念,并支持其在资源有限环境和One Health 监测中的进一步开发应用。

papers.full_text: Abstract Background Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is associated with substantial mortality, and shock with cardiac involvement is an important contributor to fatal outcomes. However, biomarker correlates, temporal trajectories, and early warning signals of clinically adjudicated cardiogenic shock (CS) in SFTS remain incompletely defined. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 775 laboratory-confirmed SFTS patients admitted to Nanjing Second Hospital from April 2020 through December 2024. Time to first clinically adjudicated CS after admission was analyzed using univariable Cox regression, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), and multivariable Cox regression. Dynamic trajectories of 6 key biomarkers over the first 14 days were assessed using locally estimated scatterplot smoothing, and restricted cubic spline models were used to characterize continuous exposure-response relationships. Results Clinically adjudicated CS occurred in 143 patients (18.5%); among 164 in-hospital deaths, 99 (60.4%) occurred in patients with CS. Elevated interleukin-6, N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide, urea, fibrin/fibrinogen degradation products, and triglycerides were independently associated with increased CS risk, whereas total cholesterol showed an inverse association. Most CS events clustered within the first week after admission, with approximately 85% occurring by day 7. Biomarker trajectory analyses showed sustained increases in inflammatory, cardiac, renal, and coagulation markers in patients who developed CS, whereas lipid markers showed a time-dependent decline. Conclusions In SFTS, clinically adjudicated CS clusters early after admission and reflects multisystem dysregulation involving inflammatory, cardiac, renal, coagulation, and lipid pathways. A six-biomarker panel may support early recognition of high-risk patients and help define a clinically relevant surveillance window during the first week of hospitalization, although external validation and more objective cardiac assessment are needed before routine implementation. analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the relationship between biomarker trajectories and the early risk of clinically adjudicated cardiogenic shock (CS) in patients with severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS). The research highlights that CS occurs predominantly within the first week of admission, with most events occurring by day 7. Key findings show that elevated levels of interleukin-6, N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide, urea, fibrin/fibrinogen degradation products, and triglycerides are independently associated with increased CS risk, while total cholesterol shows an inverse association. The study suggests that a six-biomarker panel could aid in identifying high-risk patients early, although further validation and objective cardiac assessments are required. The evidence is moderate due to the observational design and potential for confounding factors, and the study's limitations include the need for external validation and more precise cardiac evaluation.

elements_en.research_question_and_background: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is associated with substantial mortality, and shock with cardiac involvement is an important contributor to fatal outcomes. However, biomarker correlates, temporal trajectories, and early warning signals of clinically adjudicated cardiogenic shock (CS) in SFTS remain incompletely defined.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: We retrospectively analyzed 775 laboratory-confirmed SFTS patients admitted to Nanjing Second Hospital from April 2020 through December 2024. The requirement for informed consent was waived because of the retrospective design and anonymized data collection.
elements_en.methods: Time to first clinically adjudicated CS after admission was analyzed using univariable Cox regression, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), and multivariable Cox regression. Dynamic trajectories of 6 key biomarkers over the first 14 days were assessed using locally estimated scatterplot smoothing, and restricted cubic spline models were used to characterize continuous exposure-response relationships.
elements_en.main_results: Clinically adjudicated CS occurred in 143 patients (18.5%); among 164 in-hospital deaths, 99 (60.4%) occurred in patients with CS. Biomarker trajectory analyses showed sustained increases in inflammatory, cardiac, renal, and coagulation markers in patients who developed CS, whereas lipid markers showed a time-dependent decline.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: In SFTS, clinically adjudicated CS clusters early after admission and reflects multisystem dysregulation involving inflammatory, cardiac, renal, coagulation, and lipid pathways.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: A six-biomarker panel may support early recognition of high-risk patients and help define a clinically relevant surveillance window during the first week of hospitalization.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is retrospective, and external validation and more objective cardiac assessment are needed before routine implementation. The evidence is moderate due to the observational nature and potential for confounding factors.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 严重发热伴血小板减少综合征(发热伴血小板减少综合征)与高死亡率相关,心脏休克是导致致命结果的重要因素。然而,发热伴血小板减少综合征中临床判定的心源性休克(CS)的生物标志物相关性、时间轨迹和早期预警信号尚未完全定义。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们从2020年4月至2024年12月在南京二院收治的775例实验室确诊的发热伴血小板减少综合征患者中进行了回顾性分析。由于回顾性设计和匿名数据收集,不需要知情同意。
elements_zh.methods: 入院后首次临床判定的心源性休克的时间分析使用了单变量Cox回归、最小绝对收缩和选择算子(LASSO)和多变量Cox回归。使用局部加权散点图平滑法评估了前14天内6个关键生物标志物的动力学轨迹,并使用限制立方样条模型表征连续暴露-反应关系。
elements_zh.main_results: 临床判定的心源性休克发生在143名患者(18.5%)中;在164例院内死亡患者中,99例(60.4%)为CS患者。生物标志物轨迹分析显示,发展为CS的患者中炎症、心脏、肾脏和凝血标志物持续升高,而脂质标志物显示时间依赖性下降。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在发热伴血小板减少综合征中,临床判定的心源性休克在入院早期聚集,并反映了涉及炎症、心脏、肾脏、凝血和脂质途径的多系统失调。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 六项生物标志物组合可能支持高风险患者的早期识别,并有助于定义医院化第一周内的临床相关监测窗口。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究为回顾性研究,需要外部验证和更客观的心脏评估才能常规实施。证据等级为中等,由于观察性质和潜在混杂因素的存在。

papers.abstract_zh: 方法 我们从2020年4月至2024年12月在南京二院收治的775例实验室确诊的发热伴血小板减少综合征患者中进行了回顾性分析。结果 临床判定的心源性休克(CS)发生在143名患者(18.5%)中;在164例院内死亡患者中,99例(60.4%)为CS患者。资金支持 本研究由项目JSJK2026M00016资助,项目名称为“基于联邦学习的发热伴血小板减少综合征重症监护和免疫精准干预系统研究:医疗预防合作下的诊断和治疗通路优化”。伦理声明 本研究经南京二院伦理委员会审查批准(批准号2024-LS-ky056)。研究符合赫尔辛基宣言。摘要 背景 严重发热伴血小板减少综合征(发热伴血小板减少综合征)与高死亡率相关,心脏休克是导致致命结果的重要因素。然而,发热伴血小板减少综合征中临床判定的心源性休克(CS)的生物标志物相关性、时间轨迹和早期预警信号尚未完全定义。入院后首次临床判定的心源性休克的时间分析使用了单变量Cox回归、最小绝对收缩和选择算子(LASSO)和多变量Cox回归。使用局部加权散点图平滑法评估了前14天内6个关键生物标志物的动力学轨迹,并使用限制立方样条模型表征连续暴露-反应关系。升高的白细胞介素-6、N末端前B型钠尿肽、尿素、纤维蛋白/纤维蛋白原降解产物和甘油三酯与增加的心源性休克风险独立相关,而总胆固醇显示时间依赖性下降。

papers.title: Cleavage-gated Cas13-to-DNA nanostructure transduction for target-preamplification-free viral RNA detection
papers.abstract: CRISPR-Cas13a enables programmable RNA recognition without target nucleic-acid preamplification, but conventional assays encode collateral RNase activity by cleaving fluorescent reporters. Here, we developed a cleavage-gated strategy that converts transient Cas13a cleavage into a sequence-defined, strand-displacement-competent DNA actuator, shifting signal encoding from cumulative reporter intensity to a discrete scaffold topology. A chimeric masking hairpin (CMH) links Cas13a to a DNA nanostructure sensor (DNA-NS) by using a cleavable RNA loop to constrain a DNA-key bearing a pre-exposed toehold. Target-activated Cas13a cleaves the loop, converting the partially masked key into a strand-displacement-competent intermediate that reconfigures an M13mp18 scaffold from a linear to a looped state, producing a distinct electrophoretic mobility signature. Screening of 40 CMH-sensor-handle combinations identified a 4-nt toehold paired with an 18-nt sensor handle as the best-performing configuration within the tested design space (component-level ΔΔG = -1.19 kcal/mol at 37 °C). Using pooled crRNAs targeting the S, M, and L genomic segments of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV), the assay detected the lowest tested input concentration of 10.38 fM in all three replicates. In a retrospective case-control evaluation of 87 plasma-derived RNA samples, the assay agreed with RT-qPCR for 45 of 47 positive specimens and 40 healthy controls, yielding a positive percent agreement of 95.7% and a negative percent agreement of 100%. Replacing the crRNAs redirected recognition to Hantaan virus reference RNA without redesigning the CMH or DNA-NS. This work establishes a modular framework for topology-resolved viral RNA detection without target preamplification.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 在这里,我们开发了一种裂解调控策略,将Cas13a的瞬时裂解转化为一种序列定义、能够进行链置换的DNA执行器,将信号编码从累积报告分子强度转移到离散的支架拓扑结构。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在对87份来源于血浆的RNA样本进行回顾性病例对照评估中,该检测方法在47份阳性样本中的45份以及40份健康对照样本中均与RT-qPCR结果一致,得出阳性符合率为95.7%,阴性符合率为100%。

papers.title_zh: 基于裂解调控的Cas13a与DNA纳米结构转导技术实现无需靶标预扩增的病毒RNA检测
papers.source_body_en: CRISPR-Cas13a enables programmable RNA recognition without target nucleic-acid preamplification, but conventional assays encode collateral RNase activity by cleaving fluorescent reporters. Here, we developed a cleavage-gated strategy that converts transient Cas13a cleavage into a sequence-defined, strand-displacement-competent DNA actuator, shifting signal encoding from cumulative reporter intensity to a discrete scaffold topology. A chimeric masking hairpin (CMH) links Cas13a to a DNA nanostructure sensor (DNA-NS) by using a cleavable RNA loop to constrain a DNA-key bearing a pre-exposed toehold. Target-activated Cas13a cleaves the loop, converting the partially masked key into a strand-displacement-competent intermediate that reconfigures an M13mp18 scaffold from a linear to a looped state, producing a distinct electrophoretic mobility signature. Screening of 40 CMH-sensor-handle combinations identified a 4-nt toehold paired with an 18-nt sensor handle as the best-performing configuration within the tested design space (component-level ΔΔG = -1.19 kcal/mol at 37 °C). Using pooled crRNAs targeting the S, M, and L genomic segments of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV), the assay detected the lowest tested input concentration of 10.38 fM in all three replicates. In a retrospective case-control evaluation of 87 plasma-derived RNA samples, the assay agreed with RT-qPCR for 45 of 47 positive specimens and 40 healthy controls, yielding a positive percent agreement of 95.7% and a negative percent agreement of 100%. Replacing the crRNAs redirected recognition to Hantaan virus reference RNA without redesigning the CMH or DNA-NS. This work establishes a modular framework for topology-resolved viral RNA detection without target preamplification.
papers.abstract_zh: CRISPR-Cas13a能够在不进行靶标核酸预扩增的情况下实现可编程的RNA识别,但传统检测方法通过裂解荧光报告分子来编码旁观者RNase活性。在这里,我们开发了一种裂解调控策略,将Cas13a的瞬时裂解转化为一种序列定义、能够进行链置换的DNA执行器,将信号编码从累积报告分子强度转移到离散的支架拓扑结构。一种嵌合掩蔽发夹(CMH)通过一个可裂解的RNA环将Cas13a与DNA纳米结构传感器(DNA-NS)连接起来,该环限制了一个带有预暴露脚手架的DNA密钥。当靶标激活Cas13a时,它会裂解该环,将部分掩蔽的密钥转化为能够进行链置换的中间体,从而重新配置M13mp18支架从线性状态转变为环状状态,产生独特的电泳迁移率特征。对40种CMH-传感器-脚手架组合进行筛选,发现一种4个核苷酸的脚手架与18个核苷酸的传感器脚手架配对的配置在测试的设计空间内表现最佳(组件级ΔΔG = -1.19 kcal/mol,在37 °C条件下)。使用针对发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒(SFTSV)S、M和L基因组片段的混合crRNA,该检测方法在三个重复实验中均检测到了最低测试输入浓度10.38 fM。在对87份来源于血浆的RNA样本进行回顾性病例对照评估中,该检测方法在47份阳性样本中的45份以及40份健康对照样本中均与RT-qPCR结果一致,得出阳性符合率为95.7%,阴性符合率为100%。通过替换crRNA,无需重新设计CMH或DNA-NS即可将识别目标转向Hantaan病毒参考RNA。本研究建立了一种模块化框架,用于无需靶标预扩增的病毒RNA拓扑结构解析检测。

papers.title: Integrated proteomic and metabolomic profiling characterizes tryptophan metabolic disturbance associated with mortality in ICU-admitted SFTS patients
papers.abstract: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS), caused by Dabie bandavirus, is associated with high mortality among intensive care unit (ICU) patients; however, the integrated proteomic–metabolomic mechanisms underlying fatal outcomes remain poorly characterized. This prospective cohort study enrolled 68 patients with SFTS, who were admitted to the ICU and classified them as survivors (n = 33) or non-survivors (n = 35) according to their 28-day clinical outcomes. Untargeted metabolomic profiling using ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry and quantitative proteomic profiling using data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry were performed on plasma samples collected at ICU admission. analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to characterize the proteomic and metabolomic mechanisms underlying fatal outcomes in patients with severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) admitted to the ICU. A prospective cohort study enrolled 68 SFTS patients, classifying them as survivors or non-survivors based on 28-day clinical outcomes. Metabolomic and proteomic profiling were conducted on plasma samples collected at ICU admission. The results showed marked disruption of tryptophan metabolism, with decreased L-tryptophan and increased kynurenine and its downstream metabolites, indicating activation of the kynurenine pathway. papers.abstract_zh: 由大别山布尼亚病毒引起的发热伴血小板减少综合征(发热伴血小板减少综合征)与重症监护病房(ICU)患者高死亡率相关;然而,导致致命结局的整合蛋白质组学-代谢组学机制仍不明确。本前瞻性发热伴血小板减少综合征研究纳入了68名因发热伴血小板减少综合征而入住ICU的患者,并根据其28天的临床结局将其分为幸存者(n=33)和非幸存者(n=35)。采用超高效液相色谱-串联质谱法对ICU入院时采集的血浆样本进行非靶向代谢组学分析,并采用数据非依赖采集质谱法进行定量蛋白质组学分析。通过多变量分析、通路富集分析、相关性分析和受试者工作特征(ROC)曲线分析,识别潜在的预后生物标志物并阐明分子关联。非幸存者表现出更严重的多器官损伤和全身性炎症。代谢组学分析显示色氨酸代谢显著紊乱:L-色氨酸水平降低,而色氨酮及其下游代谢产物(色氨酮酸[KA]、3-羟基邻氨基苯甲酸[3-HAA]、黄尿酸[XA]和5-羟基吲哚乙酸[5-HIP])水平升高,提示色氨酮通路被激活。四种核心色氨酸代谢产物在预测28天死亡率时的综合曲线下面积(AUC)为0.934,并与肾功能和凝血指标相关。蛋白质组学分析鉴定了200种差异表达蛋白:幸存者中上调的蛋白富集于蛋白酶体通路,而非幸存者中上调的蛋白则富集于IL-17通路及其他炎症和免疫通路。整合分析显示,这四种色氨酸代谢产物与20种差异表达蛋白相关,其中六种在结局亚组中表现出显著关联。总体而言,色氨酸代谢紊乱与炎症蛋白质组学特征相结合可能表征致命性发热伴血小板减少综合征,所鉴定的代谢物-蛋白特征可能成为危重患者预后生物标志物和潜在治疗靶点。

A research team led by scientists at National Chung Hsing University in Taiwan, working with collaborators in Japan, the United States and Indonesia, reports in Virology Journal the development of a panel of monoclonal antibodies against the viral Gn glycoprotein and the construction of a magnetic nanoparticle-enhanced lateral flow assay capable of flagging the virus within 45 minutes. The work addresses a persistent gap in the response to SFTS: while molecular diagnostics such as reverse transcription PCR are sensitive and reliable, they depend on thermocyclers, trained personnel and cold-chain logistics that are often unavailable in the rural, agricultural settings where exposure to infected ticks is most likely. SFTSV belongs to the genus Bandavirus in the family Phenuiviridae and was first identified in China in 2009 after outbreaks of a mysterious febrile illness characterized by severe thrombocytopenia, leukopenia and, in a substantial fraction of cases, multi-organ failure. Case fatality rates in hospitalized patients have been reported in the range of several percent to more than ten percent depending on the region and cohort, and the virus has since been documented in South Korea, Japan, Vietnam and Taiwan. The pathogen circulates silently in a wide range of animals, including domestic livestock and wild mammals, with ticks of the genus Haemaphysalis serving as principal vectors. Because human infections often begin with nonspecific fever and gastrointestinal complaints, clinicians need a rapid differential diagnosis, particularly in areas where other tick-borne diseases such as scrub typhus and spotted fever rickettsiosis co-circulate. Serological assays, meanwhile, are of limited use in the acute phase because antibodies take days to appear. The new study targeted the Gn glycoprotein, one of the two mature subunits derived from the viral envelope precursor protein. Gn sits on the virion surface alongside its partner Gc and plays a central role in receptor binding and entry, making it an attractive antigen for immunodiagnostic capture. The researchers generated a panel of monoclonal antibodies against Gn and then systematically characterized each clone for immunoglobulin isotype, the epitope it recognizes, its binding affinity for the antigen and its efficiency at capturing intact virus. This characterization step is critical in lateral flow development because the assay depends on a carefully choreographed sandwich: one antibody, labeled with a visible reporter, binds the antigen in the sample, and a second antibody, immobilized in a thin line on the nitrocellulose membrane, catches the resulting complex so that it accumulates as a readable band. Study Biology Discover more Study Biology Book Lab Tests Compare Lab Gear Study Chemistry Check Symptoms From the panel, the team selected a monoclonal antibody with strong Gn recognition and antigen-capturing activity to serve as the detection antibody, conjugating it to magnetic nanoparticles that function as the visual reporter. Three additional antibodies were deployed as capture antibodies on the test line, a design choice intended to broaden the range of antigen conformations and epitopes that can be caught, thereby improving the chance that divergent viral strains or partially degraded antigen will still register. The use of multiple capture antibodies is a common strategy for coping with the genetic diversity of SFTSV, which is divided into several genotypes distributed across different geographic regions. A test that recognizes only one genotype risks false negatives in neighboring countries where another lineage predominates. Study Biology The magnetic nanoparticles themselves are the key innovation relative to conventional gold-nanoparticle lateral flow strips. Because the particles are superparamagnetic, the antibody-particle conjugates can be concentrated at the test line with an external magnet, and the resulting signal can be read either visually or with inexpensive magnetic readers, improving sensitivity without the cost of fluorescent or enzymatic detection systems. Magnetic labels are also less prone to interference from the colored constituents of blood and serum, an advantage when testing samples from animals whose sera may be hemolyzed or lipemic. In the reported configuration, the assay detected as little as 20 nanograms of recombinant Gn protein or approximately five times ten to the fifth focus-forming units of SFTSV within 45 minutes, all without requiring any specialized instrumentation at the point of care. Discover more Read Med Journals Track Biotech Order DNA Kits A notable strength of the study is the breadth of expression systems and host species used to validate the assay. The Gn-LFA detected recombinant Gn proteins produced in both mammalian and plant expression platforms, confirming that the antibodies recognize epitopes that survive different glycosylation patterns and folding environments. Plant-based expression is increasingly attractive for diagnostic reagent production because it is fast, scalable and inexpensive, and demonstrating cross-platform compatibility suggests the assay could be manufactured at low cost in the regions that need it most. The team also demonstrated compatibility across sera from multiple host species, an important property for One Health surveillance programs that screen cattle, goats, dogs, cats and wildlife in addition to suspected human cases. A single test format that works across species simplifies logistics considerably compared with assays that must be re-optimized for each animal’s immunoglobulin background. Study Biology The implications extend beyond the clinic. Because SFTSV infects ticks and a broad range of vertebrate hosts without causing obvious disease in most of them, the true geographic footprint of the virus is almost certainly wider than the map of confirmed human cases suggests. Veterinary and public health authorities need tools that can be carried into farms, slaughterhouses and field stations to sample animals quickly and cheaply. A lateral flow strip that returns a result in three-quarters of an hour, at a per-test cost measured in a few dollars, could transform the granularity of surveillance data, allowing health officials to detect viral circulation in a region before the first human cluster appears. The authors frame their work explicitly as proof of concept for such applications, positioning the Gn-LFA within the One Health paradigm that links human, animal and environmental health monitoring. Several caveats remain before the assay can move into routine use. The sensitivity reported here, while adequate for a rapid screening tool, is below that of real-time RT-PCR, so negative results in suspected human cases would still warrant confirmatory molecular testing, particularly early in infection when viremia may be low. Field validation with large panels of clinical samples from endemic areas, including samples containing other tick-borne pathogens that could provoke cross-reactivity, will be essential to establish specificity in real-world matrices. The study was published as an open-access paper that has been shared early to provide faster access to peer-reviewed, accepted research, and the published version remains subject to further editorial processing. The work was funded by the National Science and Technology Council of Taiwan with additional support from the Ministry of Education’s Higher Education Sprout Project, and the authors declare no competing interests. Even so, the study adds a concrete new tool to the diagnostic arsenal against an emerging virus for which no approved antiviral therapy or widely deployed human vaccine yet exists. Monoclonal antibodies against Gn could also find secondary uses in research and development, from antigen-capture ELISAs to immunohistochemistry and the characterization of viral glycoprotein processing. As SFTSV continues its quiet expansion across tick populations in Asia, and as related bandaviruses are discovered elsewhere in the world, the ability to detect viral antigen rapidly, cheaply and in the field will only grow in importance. The Taiwanese-led team’s combination of a well-characterized antibody panel, magnetic nanoparticle labeling and multi-epitope capture offers a template that other groups studying emerging tick-borne viruses may well follow. news.source_body_en: A research team from National Chung Hsing University in Taiwan, in collaboration with scientists in Japan, the United States, and Indonesia, has developed a rapid magnetic lateral flow test for the Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV). This test, which requires no laboratory, electricity, or specialized equipment, can detect the virus within 45 minutes by targeting the Gn glycoprotein, a key component of the viral envelope. The development addresses the limitations of current diagnostic methods, such as the reliance on reverse transcription PCR, which is not always feasible in rural areas. SFTSV, a tick-borne pathogen, has been documented in multiple countries, including China, South Korea, Japan, Vietnam, and Taiwan, with case fatality rates ranging from several percent to over ten percent. The test's design includes multiple capture antibodies to account for genetic diversity and improve detection accuracy across different viral strains and host species. While the study presents this as a proof of concept, further field validation is needed to confirm its effectiveness in real-world conditions. The implications of this innovation extend beyond clinical settings, offering potential tools for veterinary and public health surveillance in the context of the One Health approach.

news.content: Ask AIReal-time News Market Earnings CallEvent Calendar Watchlist Podcast Earnings CallEvent CalendarWatchlistPodcastMore Ask AIReal-time News WatchlistHoldingsMarketEarnings CallEvent CalendarPodcast South Korea's Hyundai Bioscience Pursues Phase 2 Trial for Deadly Tick-Borne SFTS Treatment Add preferred source 1 Hyundai Bioscience is advancing its broad-spectrum antiviral candidate XAFTY into Phase 2 clinical trials for Severe Fever with Thrombocytopenia Syndrome (SFTS), a disease with no approved treatment in South Korea. The company held a launch ceremony on the 13th and plans to submit its investigational new drug application to South Korea's Ministry of Food and Drug Safety, targeting first patient dosing by May next year. XAFTY is an oral formulation of niclosamide with improved bioavailability, leveraging safety data from approximately 300 COVID-19 patients in prior trials and animal study data showing 100% survival at reproduced exposure levels. SFTS has a cumulative fatality rate of approximately 18% in South Korea, with 280 infections and 41 deaths last year alone. Japan's Avigan received conditional approval despite failing its Phase 3 primary endpoint, underscoring the urgent need for alternatives. Hyundai Bioscience is also conducting a Phase 2/3 dengue fever trial in Vietnam and maintaining technical collaboration with U.S. government agencies. Key Elements Hyundai BioscienceXAFTYSevere Fever with Thrombocytopenia Syndrome (SFTS)NiclosamideBae Byung-joonJin Keun-wooSouth Korea's Ministry of Food and Drug SafetyAviganFujifilm Toyama ChemicalChoi Jun-yong Hyundai Bioscience is entering Phase 2 clinical trials to develop a treatment for Severe Fever with Thrombocytopenia Syndrome (SFTS), a disease with no approved therapy in South Korea. The illness, commonly known as "killer tick disease," has a cumulative fatality rate of approximately 18% in South Korea, with 280 infections and 41 deaths reported last year alone. The company held a launch ceremony for "XAFTY SFTS Clinical Development" at the Korea Press Center in central Seoul on the 13th, announcing plans to submit its Phase 2 investigational new drug (IND) application for XAFTY to South Korea's Ministry of Food and Drug Safety. First patient dosing is targeted for early May next year. XAFTY is an oral antiviral candidate that improves upon the low solubility and poor bioavailability of niclosamide, a compound known primarily as an antiparasitic agent. While niclosamide has demonstrated broad antiviral activity against multiple viruses, its low absorption rate has historically limited therapeutic development. Hyundai Bioscience says its drug delivery technology has overcome this barrier. "SFTS is a disease whose significance cannot be measured by patient numbers alone," said Bae Byung-joon, president of Hyundai Bioscience. "We must expand treatment options for patients and accumulate evidence on efficacy and safety." Clinical Rationale and Scientific Foundation Hyundai Bioscience previously conducted a Phase 2 trial of XAFTY in approximately 300 COVID-19 patients, establishing human safety and drug exposure data. In the analysis population of 293 patients, there were zero serious adverse events. The company plans to leverage this data alongside SFTS-related non-clinical research as the basis for clinical development. Choi Jun-yong, professor at Yonsei University College of Medicine who participated in XAFTY's COVID-19 clinical trial and SFTS cell experiments, explained: "In cell-based experiments using the SFTS virus, we confirmed that higher XAFTY concentrations correlated with greater inhibition of SFTS viral replication." Two independent animal studies published by external researchers also support the clinical development rationale. A 2025 study showed that while the survival rate in the standard niclosamide group was 60%, the nanoformulation group with improved oral absorption achieved 100% survival. Another study identified niclosamide's potential to reduce S100A4, an inflammation-related protein, and improve survival rates in SFTS-infected animals. Hyundai Bioscience stated it has reproduced the 100% survival exposure level with the XAFTY formulation in the same animal species, and pharmacokinetic bridging analysis of COVID-19 clinical data confirmed that average blood concentrations exceeded the SFTS virus inhibitory concentration throughout the five-day human dosing period. Choi Jin-ho, distinguished professor at Dankook University, described the drug delivery technology improving niclosamide's low solubility and bioavailability as XAFTY's core innovation, while cautioning: "Whether drug exposure achieved with the existing formulation remains effective in actual SFTS patients, and whether safety can be maintained at those concentrations, must be verified separately." Japan's Avigan Precedent and the Urgency of Development Currently, no drug has received marketing approval for SFTS treatment in South Korea. The Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency has imported and stockpiled Avigan (generic name: favipiravir), an antiviral approved in Japan. Avigan, developed by Japan's Fujifilm Toyama Chemical, was approved for SFTS in June 2024. In its Phase 3 trial, the fatality rate was 15.8%, failing to meet the pre-specified comparison threshold of 12.5%. Subsequent analysis of patient medical records revealed a fatality rate of 28.7%, suggesting the original comparison threshold may have underestimated actual mortality risk. Japanese regulators granted approval citing the lack of therapeutic alternatives. "It is the official position of Japan's Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency (PMDA) that the clinical results were insufficient to conclude efficacy was proven," said Jin Keun-woo, CEO of Hyundai Bioscience. "But we are not criticizing the approval process." He added: "Understanding the approval process reveals how desperately an SFTS treatment was needed. The priority is protecting one's own citizens, and the PMDA made this choice in a situation where its citizens faced threats without any treatment available." SFTS is a seasonal disease concentrated between April and November. The fatality rate surges to 26.1% among those aged 70 and older. Diagnosis is difficult and secondary infection risk among healthcare workers is high, making the treatment gap urgent to address. Global Expansion and Dengue Fever Trials Hyundai Bioscience is conducting a Phase 2/3 clinical trial in Vietnam for dengue fever treatment. First patient dosing began in April, with the trial evaluating XAFTY's efficacy and safety in dengue patients at the National Hospital for Tropical Diseases. With no significant safety concerns and smooth progress, both parties plan to expand enrollment to high-risk vulnerable populations including children and the elderly. Collaboration continues in the United States as well. Hyundai Bioscience USA, the first South Korean company to become a full member of the Medical CBRN Defense Consortium (MCDC), has completed joint technical reviews with approximately 40 officials and scientists from five U.S. government agencies. Discussions are ongoing to develop disease-specific solutions for future respiratory pandemics and lethal viruses such as Ebola. "South Korea has the experience of successfully developing treatments and vaccines during COVID-19 through collaboration among the government, the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety, and the medical community," Bae emphasized. "We will work with the ministry and experts to provide treatment alternatives for SFTS patients and healthcare workers in South Korea." First patient dosing is targeted for early May next year. XAFTY is an oral antiviral candidate that improves upon the low solubility and poor bioavailability of niclosamide, a compound known primarily as an antiparasitic agent. While niclosamide has demonstrated broad antiviral activity against multiple viruses, its low absorption rate has historically limited therapeutic development. Hyundai Bioscience says its drug delivery technology has overcome this barrier. "SFTS is a disease whose significance cannot be measured by patient numbers alone," said Bae Byung-joon, president of Hyundai Bioscience. "We must expand treatment options for patients and accumulate evidence on efficacy and safety." Clinical Rationale and Scientific Foundation Hyundai Bioscience previously conducted a Phase 2 trial of XAFTY in approximately 300 COVID-19 patients, establishing human safety and drug exposure data. In the analysis population of 293 patients, there were zero serious adverse events. The company plans to leverage this data alongside SFTS-related non-clinical research as the basis for clinical development. Choi Jun-yong, professor at Yonsei University College of Medicine who participated in XAFTY's COVID-19 clinical trial and SFTS cell experiments, explained: "In cell-based experiments using the SFTS virus, we confirmed that higher XAFTY concentrations correlated with greater inhibition of SFTS viral replication." Two independent animal studies published by external researchers also support the clinical development rationale. A 2025 study showed that while the survival rate in the standard niclosamide group was 60%, the nanoformulation group with improved oral absorption achieved 100% survival. Another study identified niclosamide's potential to reduce S100A4, an inflammation-related protein, and improve survival rates in SFTS-infected animals. Hyundai Bioscience stated it has reproduced the 100% survival exposure level with the XAFTY formulation in the same animal species, and pharmacokinetic bridging analysis of COVID-19 clinical data confirmed that average blood concentrations exceeded the SFTS virus inhibitory concentration throughout the five-day human dosing period. Choi Jin-ho, distinguished professor at Dankook University, described the drug delivery technology improving niclosamide's low solubility and bioavailability as XAFTY's core innovation, while cautioning: "Whether drug exposure achieved with the existing formulation remains effective in actual SFTS patients, and whether safety can be maintained at those concentrations, must be verified separately." Japan's Avigan Precedent and the Urgency of Development Currently, no drug has received marketing approval for SFTS treatment in South Korea. The Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency has imported and stockpiled Avigan (generic name: favipiravir), an antiviral approved in Japan. Avigan, developed by Japan's Fujifilm Toyama Chemical, was approved for SFTS in June 2024. In its Phase 3 trial, the fatality rate was 15.8%, failing to meet the pre-specified comparison threshold of 12.5%. Subsequent analysis of patient medical records revealed a fatality rate of 28.7%, suggesting the original comparison threshold may have underestimated actual mortality risk. Japanese regulators granted approval citing the lack of therapeutic alternatives. "It is the official position of Japan's Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency (PMDA) that the clinical results were insufficient to conclude efficacy was proven," said Jin Keun-woo, CEO of Hyundai Bioscience. "But we are not criticizing the approval process." He added: "Understanding the approval process reveals how desperately an SFTS treatment was needed. The priority is protecting one's own citizens, and the PMDA made this choice in a situation where its citizens faced threats without any treatment available." SFTS is a seasonal disease concentrated between April and November. The fatality rate surges to 26.1% among those aged 70 and older. Diagnosis is difficult and secondary infection risk among healthcare workers is high, making the treatment gap urgent to address. Global Expansion and Dengue Fever Trials Hyundai Bioscience is conducting a Phase 2/3 clinical trial in Vietnam for dengue fever treatment. First patient dosing began in April, with the trial evaluating XAFTY's efficacy and safety in dengue patients at the National Hospital for Tropical Diseases. With no significant safety concerns and smooth progress, both parties plan to expand enrollment to high-risk vulnerable populations including children and the elderly. Collaboration continues in the United States as well. Hyundai Bioscience USA, the first South Korean company to become a full member of the Medical CBRN Defense Consortium (MCDC), has completed joint technical reviews with approximately 40 officials and scientists from five U.S. government agencies. Discussions are ongoing to develop disease-specific solutions for future respiratory pandemics and lethal viruses such as Ebola. "South Korea has the experience of successfully developing treatments and vaccines during COVID-19 through collaboration among the government, the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety, and the medical community," Bae emphasized. "We will work with the ministry and experts to provide treatment alternatives for SFTS patients and healthcare workers in South Korea." news.content: U.S. News World News Korea Regional Review Latin America Region Odd News Entertainment Movies Music TV Sports NFL MLB NBA Soccer Voices Photos News US News World News Entertainment Sports Archive Almanac Trending Immigrant case Ilhan Omar Tropical Storm Trudy Ukraine, Starlink Bank of America Cat burglar MAMA Awards 3K lb. pumpkin World News Oct. 13, 2026 / 7:45 AM Hyundai Bioscience eyes Phase 2 trials for tick-borne disease drug By Tae-gyu Kim Hyundai Bioscience CEO Bae Byoung-jun speaks about the antiviral drug candidate XAFTY at a press conference in Seoul on Tuesday. Photo by Hyundai Bioscience SEOUL, Oct. 13 (UPI) -- South Korea's Hyundai Bioscience said Tuesday that the company would accelerate the development of a treatment for severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome, or SFTS, a deadly tick-borne disease for which no approved therapy is available. During a press conference in Seoul, the biopharmaceutical company disclosed its plans to advance the antiviral drug candidate XAFTY into Phase 2 clinical trials in the East Asian country. SFTS is a viral infection spread through the bites of infected ticks. The disease can trigger severe fever and a sharp decline in blood platelet levels, sometimes resulting in multiple organ failure and death. Hyundai Bioscience said that SFTS has a cumulative case fatality rate of about 18% in South Korea. In 2025, the disease claimed 41 lives among 280 reported patients nationwide for an annual fatality rate of 14.6%. The company said that the infection also poses a serious occupational risk to healthcare workers, as the virus can spread through direct contact with infected patients' blood and bodily fluids. news.content_zh: 韩国生物制药公司现代生物科技 (Hyundai Bioscience) 于 2026 年 10 月 13 日宣布,计划将其 抗病毒药物 候选药物 XAFTY 进入 2 期临床试验,用于治疗严重发热伴血小板减少综合征 (发热伴血小板减少综合征),这是一种尚未获得批准治疗的 蜱媒 疾病。发热伴血小板减少综合征 通过受感染的蜱虫叮咬传播,可导致严重发烧、血小板水平急剧下降,甚至死亡。2025年,韩国报告的280例病例中,有41人死亡,死亡率为14.6%。该公司强调医护人员的职业风险,因为病毒可以通过直接接触感染患者的血液和体液传播。虽然实验室实验表明 XAFTY 可以抑制病毒复制,但其针对 发热伴血小板减少综合征 的安全性和有效性尚未在人体试验中得到测试。该公告发布之际,现代生物科学致力于解决传染病的全球挑战,包括 发热伴血小板减少综合征,该疾病在中国、日本和其他亚洲国家也有报道。

source_language_evidence.scale_impact_and_risk: 不对,这是一篇关于SFTSV诊断技术的科学摘要。让我准确翻译:重度发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒(SFTSV)是一种新兴的蜱传人畜共患病原体,可导致人类高死亡率并在动物中隐性循环,凸显了快速、可现场部署诊断方法的必要性。现有的分子和血清学方法仍依赖于专业基础设施,限制了其在资源有限环境中的应用。本研究开发了一种针对SFTSV糖蛋白Gn(Gn)的磁性纳米颗粒增强型侧向流免疫层析试纸条(Gn-LFA),用于快速抗原检测。我们制备了一组抗Gn单克隆抗体,并系统表征了其同型、表位识别、结合亲和力和病毒捕获效率。选取了一株对Gn具有强识别和抗原捕获活性的单克隆抗体作为检测抗体,并将其偶联至磁性纳米颗粒;另外三株抗体则作为捕获抗体固定于检测线上以提高抗原识别效率。Gn-LFA可检测到哺乳动物和植物表达系统所产生的重组Gn蛋白,并展现了跨多种宿主物种血清的兼容性。该检测方法在45分钟内即可检测低至20 ng的重组Gn蛋白或约5 × 10?

A new retrospective study published in BMC Infectious Diseases now offers one of the clearest pictures yet of a particularly lethal complication: cardiogenic shock. Drawing on 775 laboratory-confirmed cases treated at Nanjing Second Hospital in China between April 2020 and December 2024, a team led by Jianshe Xu and Jing Xie traced how inflammatory, cardiac, renal, coagulation, and lipid markers behave in the days surrounding hospital admission, and used those trajectories to identify who is most likely to collapse into shock while there is still time to intervene. The stakes of the question are stark. Cardiogenic shock, a state in which the heart can no longer pump enough blood to perfuse the body’s organs, occurred in 143 of the 775 patients, or 18.5 percent. More telling is how that figure maps onto mortality. Of the 164 patients who died in the hospital, 99, or roughly six in ten, had developed clinically adjudicated cardiogenic shock. The condition was not simply a marker of severity; it was the dominant final pathway for the majority of fatal outcomes, confirming that cardiac involvement is a central driver of death in this viral hemorrhagic-fever-like syndrome rather than a bystander phenomenon. Timing proved to be one of the study’s most clinically consequential findings. The researchers found that most shock events clustered tightly within the first week after admission, with approximately 85 percent occurring by day seven. This early clustering defines what the authors describe as a clinically relevant surveillance window: a period during which intensive monitoring, aggressive fluid management, and readiness for cardiac support could plausibly alter outcomes. For clinicians managing SFTS in endemic regions of East Asia, where the disease is transmitted by ticks and, in some documented instances, through contact with infected blood, the implication is that the first seven days of hospitalization are when the battle is most often decided. Discover more Bioengineering News Subscription Bioengineering Career Guide Bioengineering Job Board iGEM Team Directory Bioengineering Events Calendar To disentangle which laboratory abnormalities genuinely predict shock, the team employed a layered statistical strategy. They began with univariable Cox regression to screen potential predictors, then applied least absolute shrinkage and selection operator analysis, a regularization technique that prunes redundant variables and guards against overfitting, before finalizing a multivariable Cox model. The result was a six-biomarker panel comprising interleukin-6, N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide, urea, fibrin and fibrinogen degradation products, triglycerides, and total cholesterol. Five of these rose with shock risk; the sixth, total cholesterol, moved in the opposite direction, with lower levels independently associated with greater danger. The biological logic embedded in that panel is worth unpacking. Interleukin-6 is a master cytokine of the innate immune response, and its elevation signals the cytokine storm widely believed to underlie much of SFTS pathology. N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide is released by stretched or stressed heart muscle, making it a sensitive chemical barometer of cardiac strain. Urea points to declining kidney function, a frequent companion of circulatory collapse. Fibrin and fibrinogen degradation products indicate uncontrolled clot formation and breakdown, the signature of disseminated intravascular coagulation, while the lipid abnormalities, rising triglycerides and falling cholesterol, suggest both deranged metabolism and the consumption of lipoproteins as they bind and neutralize circulating endotoxin-like products during severe inflammation. Because single time-point measurements can miss the dynamics of a rapidly evolving illness, the researchers also modeled biomarker trajectories over the first fourteen days using locally estimated scatterplot smoothing, a flexible nonparametric technique that reveals trends without imposing a rigid mathematical form. Patients who went on to develop shock showed sustained upward trajectories in their inflammatory, cardiac, renal, and coagulation markers, while their lipid markers declined in a time-dependent fashion. In other words, shock was not announced by a single alarming lab value but by the direction and persistence of change across multiple organ systems simultaneously, a pattern the authors frame as multisystem dysregulation. The study also applied restricted cubic spline models to characterize how continuous biomarker levels relate to shock risk. These spline approaches allow the relationship between exposure and outcome to bend and curve rather than forcing a straight line, which matters in medicine where thresholds and nonlinear dose-response relationships are common. This analytical refinement, combined with trajectory analysis, strengthens the case that the six markers capture a graded, escalating risk process rather than an arbitrary statistical association. Discover more Bioengineer Blog Access Bioengineering Research Papers Learn Engineering Track Biotech Tour Colleges Importantly, the outcome measure was not a loose laboratory surrogate. The investigators used clinically adjudicated cardiogenic shock, meaning each case was reviewed and confirmed against clinical criteria rather than inferred from billing codes or a single measurement. That adjudication process lends the 18.5 percent incidence figure and the mortality association greater credibility than many earlier reports, which have varied widely in how they defined shock in SFTS. The retrospective design and the waiver of informed consent, approved by the hospital’s ethics committee under the Declaration of Helsinki, were appropriate for the anonymized data involved. The authors are careful to note the limits of their work before it can change practice. As a single-center retrospective study, the findings require external validation in other hospitals and regions, and the authors themselves acknowledge that more objective cardiac assessment, such as direct hemodynamic measurement or echocardiographic evaluation of pump function, would strengthen future iterations of the risk model. The six-biomarker panel is best understood today as an early-warning framework, a way to flag patients whose inflammatory, cardiac, renal, coagulation, and lipid profiles are moving in the wrong direction, rather than as a finished diagnostic tool ready for routine deployment. Even so, the study arrives at a moment of growing concern about SFTS. The disease, caused by a phlebovirus in the family Phenuiviridae, continues to expand its geographic footprint in China, South Korea, Japan, and Vietnam, and case fatality rates in severe cohorts have ranged into the double digits. No licensed specific antiviral therapy exists, so management remains supportive, which makes early identification of patients at imminent risk of shock one of the few levers clinicians can currently pull. A biomarker panel that can be measured on standard hospital laboratories, combined with the knowledge that 85 percent of shock events arrive within seven days of admission, gives intensive care teams a concrete, actionable window. The work was supported by a Chinese provincial health research project focused on SFTS intensive care and immune precision intervention under a medical-prevention collaboration framework, and the open-access publication ensures the findings are immediately available to clinicians across the affected region. If validated externally, this multisystem biomarker approach could shift SFTS care from reactive management of established shock toward anticipatory protection of the heart during the vulnerable first week of illness. analysis.time: The study was published on October 14, 2026. The event date range is from April 2020 to December 2024, with most shock events occurring within the first week after admission, particularly by day seven.
analysis.location_and_population: The study was conducted at Nanjing Second Hospital in China, involving 775 laboratory-confirmed cases of Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) between April 2020 and December 2024.
analysis.event: A retrospective study published in BMC Infectious Diseases identified cardiogenic shock as a dominant final pathway for fatal outcomes in SFTS patients, with 143 patients (18.5%) developing the condition and 99 of them (60%) dying in the hospital.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Cardiogenic shock occurred in 143 of 775 patients, or 18.5 percent, and was associated with 99 deaths, or approximately 60 percent of all fatalities. The condition was found to be a central driver of death rather than a bystander phenomenon.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The study used a layered statistical strategy, including univariable Cox regression, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator analysis, and multivariable Cox modeling. The findings require external validation and more objective cardiac assessments, such as direct hemodynamic measurement or echocardiographic evaluation, for future refinement.

analysis.brief_en: A new study published in BMC Infectious Diseases on October 14, 2026, highlights the critical role of cardiogenic shock in the fatal outcomes of Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) patients. The research, conducted at Nanjing Second Hospital in China, analyzed 775 laboratory-confirmed cases from April 2020 to December 2024. It found that 143 patients (18.5%) developed cardiogenic shock, with 99 of them (60%) dying in the hospital. The study identified a six-biomarker panel, including interleukin-6 and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide, that correlates with shock risk. Most shock events occurred within the first week of admission, with 85% happening by day seven. The findings suggest that early monitoring and intervention during the first seven days could significantly impact patient outcomes. However, the study is a single-center retrospective analysis and requires external validation. The authors emphasize the need for more objective cardiac assessments to refine the risk model further.

news.content: 주요서비스 바로가기 본문 바로가기 매체정보 바로가기 로그인 바로가기 기사검색 바로가기 전체서비스 바로가기 Thursday, October 15, 2026 Privacy Contact Us About Us Code of Ethics Login Subscription Mobile 전체메뉴 버튼 Latest News Business CEOs Finance Diplomacy Book Entertainment Technology Others 검색버튼 기사검색 검색 이전 기사보기 다음 기사보기 Hyundai Bioscience seeks swift clinical trials for tick-borne disease treatment 스크롤 이동 상태바 홈 Technology Business CEOs Finance Diplomacy Book Entertainment Others 미분류 Hyundai Bioscience seeks swift clinical trials for tick-borne disease treatment 기자명 Tim Kim Published 2026.10.13 13:13 페이스북(으)로 기사보내기 트위터(으)로 기사보내기 URL복사(으)로 기사보내기 기사저장 다른 공유 찾기 Korean biotech firm plans Phase 2 trials of antiviral drug Xafty Hyundai Bioscience CEO Bae Byoung-jun speaks during a press conference about the anti-viral drug XAFTY in Seoul on Oct. 13. South Korea’s Hyundai Bioscience announced on Oct. 13 that it plans to accelerate the development of a treatment for severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS). It is a potentially fatal tick-borne infectious disease for which no approved treatment is currently available, according to Hyundai Bioscience. The biopharmaceutical firm disclosed its plans at a press conference in Seoul, saying it intends to launch Phase 2 clinical trials in the country using its antiviral drug candidate XAFTY. SFTS is a viral disease primarily transmitted through bites from infected ticks. It can cause high fever, gastrointestinal symptoms, and a sharp decline in blood platelet counts, potentially leading to multiple organ failure and death. The disease has a cumulative case fatality rate of about 18 percent in South Korea, according to the company. Last year, 41 of the 280 reported SFTS patients in the country died, representing a fatality rate of 14.6 percent. The disease also poses risks to healthcare workers who come into contact with infected patients’ blood or bodily fluids. In July 2025, seven healthcare workers in the central South Korean city of Cheongju reportedly contracted SFTS after being exposed to the blood or bodily fluids of an infected patient during treatment. Hyundai Bioscience said that laboratory studies of XAFTY had demonstrated its ability to inhibit viral replication, raising hopes that the drug could be developed into a treatment for SFTS. However, the company has yet to establish the drug’s safety and effectiveness against SFTS in human clinical trials. Dankook University Prof. Choy Jin-ho said that XAFTY is based on niclosamide. He has developed a proprietary drug delivery technology to help come up with XAFTY. Niclosamide has been used as an antiparasitic drug for more than 60 years, and its efficacy and safety are well established, according to him. “Despite its strong antiviral properties, its clinical application has been limited by its inability to maintain sufficient concentrations in the bloodstream when taken orally,” Choy said. “We have overcome this limitation through our proprietary technology.” Yonsei University Prof. Choi Jun-yong said that XAFTY can potentially become a platform drug to deal with various diseases. “Niclosamide has demonstrated effectiveness against 33 viral diseases, but its poor absorption has been a major obstacle. XAFTY has effectively addressed this problem, as demonstrated in clinical trials involving COVID-19 patients,” he said. “The clinical trial results showed that viral levels declined 13.5 times faster in the treatment group than in the control group, while symptom improvement occurred five days earlier. No serious adverse events were reported.” Hyundai Bioscience CEO Bae Byoung-jun said that the company would work closely with the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety to expedite the launch of Phase 2 clinical trials of XAFTY. news.source_body_en: Hyundai Bioscience, a South Korean biotech firm, announced on October 13, 2026, its plan to accelerate the development of a treatment for severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS), a potentially fatal tick-borne disease. The company intends to launch Phase 2 clinical trials of its antiviral drug candidate XAFTY, which has shown laboratory effectiveness against SFTS. However, the drug's safety and efficacy in human trials have not yet been confirmed. SFTS has a case fatality rate of approximately 18 percent in South Korea, with 41 of 280 reported patients dying last year. The disease poses a risk to healthcare workers exposed to infected patients’ blood or bodily fluids. XAFTY is based on niclosamide, an antiparasitic drug with established safety, but its poor oral absorption has been a challenge. The company claims to have overcome this limitation through proprietary technology, as demonstrated in trials involving COVID-19 patients. The clinical trial results for XAFTY showed faster viral decline and earlier symptom improvement in the treatment group, but no serious adverse events were reported. Hyundai Bioscience is collaborating with the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety to expedite the process.

news.content_title: Visual guide to help researchers track Asian longhorned tick
news.content: A shot of the Asian longhorned tick, a species that has recently invaded the United States. (Photo courtesy of James Gathany/CDC)Ever since the Asian longhorned tick (Haemaphysalis longicornis) was officially reported in New Jersey two years ago, researchers have sought to understand the threat this self-cloning species poses to human and animal health. Native to eastern Asia and Australia/New Zealand, where it transmits disease to both humans and livestock, H. longicornis has now been reported in multiple U.S. states: Arkansas, Connecticut, Delaware, Kentucky, Maryland, North Carolina, New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania, Tennessee, Virginia and West Virginia. Getting a handle on this tick species has been difficult so far, largely because it is nearly identical to the rabbit tick (Haemaphysalis leporispalustrisis) and the bird tick (Haemaphysalis chordeilis), both of which are mostly harmless to humans, according to Rutgers Today. To assist surveillance efforts, a collaborative research team, including members of the Rutgers Center for Vector Biology, has created a visual guide. “To begin to understand the threat posed by Asian longhorned ticks in the U.S., we need to know the full extent of its distribution,” lead author of the guide Andrea Egizi, PhD, a visiting professor at Rutgers' Center for Vector Biology and a research scientist with the Monmouth County Tick-borne Disease Program, tells Rutgers Today. “We made this key so that researchers across the country have an easier way to identify [longhorned ticks].” When these ticks actually got here Thanks to the new guide, researchers now know that the Asian longhorn tick was actually spotted in the U.S. a lot earlier than previously believed. “... the Asian longhorned tick has been present in New Jersey since at least 2013, but that first discovery, found on a dog in Union County, was initially mistaken for a rabbit tick,” Dina Fonseca, PhD contributing author of the guide and director of the Rutgers Center for Vector Biology, told Rutgers Today. The guide, published in ZooKeys, allows researchers to distinguish all life stages of the four Haemaphysalis species that may be encountered in North America. It specifically pinpoints their unique physical traits, such as hornlike spurs on the adult Asian longhorned tick's mouthparts. These characteristics are apparent on scanning electron microscopic images taken by the research team's collaborators. “This tool will also help to improve our understanding of the biology and ecology of native Haemaphysalis species, which have been relatively poorly studied compared with other native ixodids,” the researchers say in the guide. Although the Asian longhorned tick is largely considered a livestock pest, it can cause severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome as well as other diseases in humans, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. As of August 1, 2019, no harmful germs that can infect people have been found in the ticks collected in the United States, but research on this and other species is ongoing. “Careful monitoring to detect the potential arrival of other members of this genus is encouraged. Should additional Haemaphysalis species establish themselves in North America, this key will require revision,” the researchers conclude

news.source_body_en: The article, published on October 9, 2026, discusses the Asian longhorned tick (Haemaphysalis longicornis), which was first reported in New Jersey in 2013. Researchers have created a visual guide to help identify this tick, which is nearly identical to the rabbit tick and bird tick, both of which are generally harmless to humans. The guide, published in ZooKeys, highlights unique physical traits such as hornlike spurs on the adult tick's mouthparts. The tick is a self-cloning species that has spread to multiple U.S. states, including Arkansas, Connecticut, Delaware, Kentucky, Maryland, North Carolina, New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania, Tennessee, Virginia, and West Virginia. While it is primarily a livestock pest, it can cause severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome and other diseases in humans. As of August 1, 2019, no harmful germs infecting humans were found in U.S. ticks, but ongoing research is necessary to monitor potential risks. The guide also emphasizes the need for careful monitoring to detect the arrival of other Haemaphysalis species, which may require future revisions.

Photo by Hyundai Bioscience SEOUL, Oct. 13 (UPI) -- South Korea's Hyundai Bioscience said Tuesday that the company would accelerate the development of a treatment for severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome, or SFTS, a deadly tick-borne disease for which no approved therapy is available. During a press conference in Seoul, the biopharmaceutical company disclosed its plans to advance the antiviral drug candidate XAFTY into Phase 2 clinical trials in the East Asian country. SFTS is a viral infection spread through the bites of infected ticks. The disease can trigger severe fever and a sharp decline in blood platelet levels, sometimes resulting in multiple organ failure and death. Hyundai Bioscience said that SFTS has a cumulative case fatality rate of about 18% in South Korea. In 2025, the disease claimed 41 lives among 280 reported patients nationwide for an annual fatality rate of 14.6%. The company said that the infection also poses a serious occupational risk to healthcare workers, as the virus can spread through direct contact with infected patients' blood and bodily fluids. According to Hyundai Bioscience, laboratory experiments have shown that XAFTY could suppress viral replication, suggesting its potential as a treatment for SFTS. However, the drug's safety and efficacy against SFTS have yet to be tested in human clinical trials. The Seoul-based firm noted that SFTS has been reported mostly in China, Japan, and South Korea, with cases also identified in other Asian countries, including Vietnam, Myanmar, Thailand, and Pakistan. "We have felt a profound sense of responsibility over the continued loss of life and infections among healthcare workers while our clinical development was delayed, despite having completed laboratory studies several years ago," CEO Bae Byoung-jun said. "Having developed a platform technology with the potential to address infectious diseases worldwide, we concluded that we could no longer overlook the challenges facing medical professionals in South Korea," he added. The share price of Hyundai Bioscience rose 1.42% on the Seoul bourse on Tuesday, while the benchmark KOSPI declined 5.46%. Hyundai Bioscience is the parent company of Penetrium Bioscience, which is also working on antiviral drugs.
